What We Do

Full-Service Neurology Revenue Cycle Management

Neurology billing combines high-complexity E/M coding, diagnostic procedure billing for EEG and EMG, infusion administration for MS biologics and migraine preventives, and prior authorization management for specialty neurological agents. PMEX manages every revenue stream inside your existing EHR.

Neurology E/M Coding

New and established neurology visit E/M coded from 2021 MDM at correct complexity.

EEG Billing

Routine EEG (95816), extended EEG (95819), and ambulatory EEG (95953) coded correctly.

EMG and NCS Billing

Nerve conduction studies (95907 to 95913) and EMG (95860 to 95872) billed per muscle group.

MS Infusion Billing

Natalizumab, ocrelizumab, and other MS biologics billed with J-code and prior auth.

Botox for Migraine

OnabotulinumtoxinA (J0585) and injection codes billed per unit for chronic migraine.

Epilepsy Monitoring

Long-term EEG monitoring (95950 to 95953) and video-EEG billed per day of recording.

Sound Familiar?

Common Neurology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

EEG billed at routine level when the extended or ambulatory study was performed.

PMEX codes EEG from the report methodology: routine, extended, asleep/awake, or ambulatory per CPT descriptor.

Botox for chronic migraine units underbilled when fewer than 155 units are submitted.

PMEX verifies units injected from the procedure note and bills J0585 per unit administered, confirmed against the injection site documentation.

MS biologic prior authorization not renewed before the next infusion cycle.

PMEX tracks biologic auth expiration per patient and initiates renewal 14 days before the next scheduled infusion.

EMG billed for more muscles than documented in the procedure report.

PMEX codes EMG from the procedure report, counting documented muscles per limb and applying the correct CPT code range.

Neurology consultation billed as an established office visit, losing the higher initial rate.

PMEX applies the correct new patient or initial consultation code for every first-contact neurology evaluation.

Stroke care inpatient coding defaulted to a low-level subsequent visit.

PMEX codes inpatient neurology visits from MDM complexity, capturing level 3 on high-acuity stroke management days.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Neurology Billing

Neurology practices lose 15 to 24 percent of revenue to EEG miscoding, EMG over-reporting, and biologic authorization gaps.

PATTERN 01

EEG Billed at Wrong Level

Ambulatory EEG performed over 24 hours (95953). Billing team submits routine EEG (95816, $85). Correct: ambulatory EEG (95953, $210). $125 per study lost when methodology is not read from the report.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes EEG from the study report, confirming the type of EEG performed: routine, sleep-deprived, extended, or ambulatory, and applying the correct CPT code per the methodology described in the report.

PATTERN 02

Botox Units Underbilled for Chronic Migraine

155 units of onabotulinumtoxinA administered across 31 injection sites per the PREEMPT protocol. Billing team submits 100 units of J0585. 55 units of drug revenue lost per treatment session, occurring every 12 weeks.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX verifies the total units injected from the procedure note and submits J0585 at the exact unit count documented, alongside the injection administration CPT codes per the number of sites injected.

PATTERN 03

MS Biologic Infusion Denied, Authorization Expired

Ocrelizumab infusion administered on the 6-month cycle. Prior authorization expired 10 days prior. No one initiated the renewal. $14,000 drug claim denied. Retroactive authorization not available under the commercial payer contract.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks biologic authorization expiration per patient and initiates renewal 14 days before the scheduled infusion date, with the required clinical documentation of EDSS score and treatment response attached.

Questions

Neurology Billing Questions Answered

We read the study report to confirm the type of EEG performed. Routine EEG (95816) is 20 to 40 minutes awake. Extended EEG includes sleep. Ambulatory EEG (95953) is recorded over 24 or more hours. The CPT code follows the methodology, not the order.

NCS codes (95907 to 95913) are billed per the number of nerve conduction studies performed. EMG codes (95860 to 95872) are billed per the number of muscles studied. We count from the procedure report.

We bill J0585 per unit of onabotulinumtoxinA administered, verified from the procedure note, alongside the injection administration codes. Coverage requires a diagnosis of chronic migraine (G43.709) and prior authorization on most commercial plans.

Yes. We manage the initial authorization and every renewal cycle, including the clinical documentation of EDSS score, relapse history, and prior treatment trials required by commercial payers.

Yes. Long-term EEG monitoring codes (95950 to 95953) are billed per day of recording. We coordinate with the EMU nursing team to confirm the monitoring days documented.
